feature_facts: The DevTools onboarding view model is located at devtools/pay-card/src/usePayCardViewModel.ts; its public return object retains the onboarding, steps, completedCount, totalCount, allDone, toggleStep, and setAllSteps fields, which callers use to render and modify the checklist.
Host binding is provided by devtools/bindings/src/usePayCardToolProps.ts; public flags retain payTabEnabled and setCardParam, and pass the same onboarding contract to the Pay Card tool.

The fixed navigation entry points for the DevTools cross-platform control are devtools/pay-card/src/components/Section/Section.web.tsx and devtools/pay-card/src/components/ToggleRow/ToggleRow.native.tsx; the Web Section container continues to use flex flex-col gap-12.

The public entry points for the feature tour are fixed as features/flow/pay-card-feature-tour/src/components/FeatureTour/useFeatureTourViewModel.ts and features/flow/pay-card-feature-tour/src/state/slice.ts; the view model retains isVisible, onShown, and onDismiss.

The Balance page's public navigation entry points are fixed as features/flow/pay-card-balance/src/logic/aggregateBalance.ts, features/flow/pay-card-balance/src/logic/buildBalanceFilterOptions.ts, and features/flow/pay-card-balance/src/components/ActionTiles/useActionTilesViewModel.ts, and the quick actions view model returns tiles.
formatId formats kyc-check as Kyc check and bridge-check as Bridge check; only tokenizable ID undergoes the initial-letter display conversion, and whitespace-only input is returned unchanged.
The DevTools onboarding's stable step order is kyc, claim, topup, walletPay, purchase; the host and UI must not each maintain their own separate order.

When the native platform calls setCardParam, it dispatches an override with key lwmPayTab to featureFlags/setOverride; the payload retains enabled=true and only updates params.card to the passed boolean value.
Web Section wraps the title and children in a semantic section element; both the title and child content must appear in the final markup rather than remain in the wrapper component's props.
The Web Section content container must retain the flex flex-col gap-12 class combination to preserve the vertical layout and established spacing.
The native ToggleRow renders both label and description and renders the boolean toggle as a controlled input with type="checkbox"; checked directly reflects the passed state.
toggleStep only toggles the done value of the matched step; setAllSteps only emits changes for steps not yet in the target state, and steps already in that state must not be written again.
The feature tour state starts with hasSeenFeatureTour=false; restore accepts only a boolean hasSeenFeatureTour, and invalid persisted values such as strings must not overwrite the existing state.
The balance filter starts at all; restore accepts only a non-empty string balanceFilter, and an empty string or missing value must not clear the currently valid selection.

aggregateBalance returns ready when there is neither loading nor an error; loading and error signals take precedence over the balance value when determining the state, and the caller-provided filterOptions and confirmation callback are preserved.

aggregateBalance first resolves the effective filter, then sums the value of matching stablecoins by currency id or the filter option's ticker; stableBalance is the filtered sum, while hasBalance indicates whether any of the current holdings have a positive balance.
resolveSelection keeps the current selection only if it is in the candidate ID list; Invalid Selection Fallback to all, falling back to the first available option if all is also absent.

buildBalanceFilterOptions puts all first, merges the default stablecoins with actual holdings by ticker, and appends any remaining held currencies after the default options without creating duplicates.

Balance filter options use a stable currency id as the selection value; held default currencies use the default market name as their title and the corresponding holding's fiat value as countervalue, while other holdings also retain their own countervalues.

useFeatureTourViewModel returns isVisible=true if the user has not yet seen the tour; the title, description, line items, and CTA copy are supplied by the host and preserved unchanged in the visible model.
When the feature tour is actually shown, onShown first sends a screen event with the page identifier fixed at Page card feature intro; a re-render alone must not count as the tour being shown.
When the user performs onDismiss, first dispatch the viewed state, then report button_clicked with the fixed parameters button=got it and page=$page; the close action is not equivalent to onShown.

The feature tour slice provides three kinds of state transition—mark, reset, and restore: mark sets the value to true, reset sets it to false, and restore still accepts only a boolean hasSeenFeatureTour.
CardApiExtraSchema accepts non-empty cardApiBaseUrl and cardBaanxClientKey, plus a callable token getter and a callable refreshCardSession; an empty URL or non-function callback must be rejected.

Card API awaits refreshCardSession and retries once with the refreshed token only if the initial request fails authentication; after schema parsing, CardApiExtra still retains the refreshCardSession function reference supplied by the caller.

The tiles returned by useActionTilesViewModel retain each tile's id, label, and business-logic onPress; the wrapper must not drop the business-logic callback or invoke it prematurely during hook construction.

When a user clicks a quick-action tile, useActionTilesViewModel must first report button_clicked, with parameters including the tile id, buttonLocation=quick_action, and the current page, then call the tile's original onPress.

Both Desktop and Mobile persist the feature tour's viewed state and the balance filter state together under the payCard storage key, and dispatch each state to its respective slice during startup restoration; any update to either slice must save a combined snapshot.
Desktop and Mobile DevTools both register the pay-card tool, but the native host explicitly passes platform=native; the Pay Tab host wires up the balance, feature tour, and quick actions view models.

All new packages retain the web/native entry point and public exports, and the application layer consumes them only through package boundaries; the implementation must not change unrelated feature flags, asset blacklists, or existing storage key behavior.

voice.operating_principle: Reproduce via the actual package exports, host calls, and Redux restore chain first, then break cross-platform differences into small, verifiable findings.
voice.handoff_rule: Handoffs must include the call path, input state, actual output, and corresponding owner—not just a final screenshot or a verbal conclusion.
voice.closure_rule: Only close after someone other than the implementer has reviewed the same behavior boundaries, failure counterexamples, and persistence fallbacks on both Desktop and Mobile.

disclosures.contract: The public return container of usePayCardViewModel must provide completedCount, totalCount, and allDone together; callers should no longer infer these aggregate fields from the private step array.

refreshCardSession is awaited only after the first authentication failure, and after refreshing the token, it retries the original Card API request at most once; normal requests must not refresh proactively.
The click wrapper for useActionTilesViewModel must first emit button_clicked with the quick_action position, then invoke the tile's original business callback; the order must be observable.

Once validation of CardApiExtraSchema succeeds, the caller-provided refreshCardSession function reference and the remaining extra fields must be preserved; they must not be wrapped in a new, non-comparable container.
